ui_bugs.issue: FIXED by testing agent. useEffect(load,[id]) at StrategyCenter.jsx:575 was receiving a callback that returned a Promise (from `api.libraryGet(id).then(...).catch(...)`). React treated the Promise as a cleanup function, crashing on unmount with 'destroy is not a function'. Any click on a catalog card produced a red-screen uncaught runtime error. Patched to `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [id]);`. Retested: catalog-detail renders with catalog-favorite/catalog-regrade/catalog-back.

rca of the issue: CRITICAL FRONTEND CRASH — /app/frontend/src/pages/StrategyCenter.jsx:575 (before fix): `const load = () => api.libraryGet(id).then(...).catch(...); useEffect(load, [id]);`. Because `load` is a bodyless arrow, it returns the promise chain from .then().catch(). React's useEffect expects the callback to return either undefined or a cleanup function. When React tries to run the returned 'cleanup' (a Promise) during unmount / dep change, it calls it as a function, producing 'TypeError: destroy is not a function'. Consequence: every click on a library catalog card produced a red-screen uncaught runtime error and the CatalogDetail never rendered. Mitigation applied: wrap in block-body `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [id]);`. Verified fix by re-clicking library-open-turtle → catalog-detail rendered fully with all 3 action buttons.
